groups.name: Austin Yogurt Shop Murders
groups.description: Wrongful convictions arising from the 1991 Austin, Texas yogurt shop murders investigation.

groups.name: Beatrice Six
groups.description: Six individuals wrongfully convicted of the 1985 murder of Helen Wilson in Beatrice, Nebraska, exonerated by DNA evidence in 2009.

groups.name: Central Park Five (The Exonerated Five)
groups.description: Five Black and Latino teenagers wrongfully convicted of the 1989 Central Park jogger assault in New York City, exonerated in 2002.

groups.name: Chicago 7
groups.description: Anti-war activists tried on federal conspiracy and incitement charges following the 1968 Democratic National Convention protests.

groups.name: Cleveland Martyrs
groups.description: Ricky Jackson, Wiley Bridgeman, and Kwame Ajamu (Ronnie Bridgeman), wrongfully convicted of a 1975 Cleveland murder based on coerced child testimony.

groups.name: Dixmoor Five
groups.description: Five teenagers wrongfully convicted of the 1991 murder of Cateresa Matthews in Dixmoor, Illinois, exonerated by DNA in 2011.

groups.name: Ford Heights Four
groups.description: Four men wrongfully convicted of a 1978 double murder in Ford Heights, Illinois, exonerated by DNA evidence in 1996.

groups.name: Fort Stewart Soldiers
groups.description: Three U.S. Army soldiers wrongfully convicted in connection with a 1992 murder near Fort Stewart, Georgia.

groups.name: Groveland Four
groups.description: Four young Black men falsely accused of rape in Lake County, Florida in 1949; posthumously pardoned and exonerated.

groups.name: Harlem Park Three
groups.description: Alfred Chestnut, Ransom Watkins, and Andrew Stewart Jr., wrongfully convicted as teenagers in Baltimore in 1983 and exonerated in 2019.

groups.name: Jena Six
groups.description: Six Black high school students charged with attempted murder in Jena, Louisiana in 2006 amid racial tensions.

groups.name: MOVE 9
groups.description: Nine members of the MOVE organization convicted of third-degree murder following a 1978 Philadelphia police standoff.

groups.name: Norfolk Four
groups.description: Four U.S. Navy sailors coerced into false confessions for a 1997 murder in Norfolk, Virginia; pardoned in 2017.

groups.name: NYC Subway Token Booth Murder
groups.description: Three young men wrongfully convicted of the 1995 firebombing of a Brooklyn subway token booth.

groups.name: Scottsboro Boys
groups.description: Nine Black teenagers falsely accused of rape in Alabama in 1931; a landmark civil rights and wrongful conviction case.

groups.name: Tulia 47
groups.description: Mass wrongful drug arrests in Tulia, Texas in 1999 fabricated by a corrupt undercover officer; most defendants were pardoned in 2003.

groups.name: West Memphis Three
groups.description: Damien Echols, Jason Baldwin, and Jessie Misskelley Jr., convicted in 1994 during the Satanic Panic and released via Alford pleas in 2011.

groups.name: Chelsea Four
groups.description: Four men framed by the FBI for a 1965 murder in Chelsea, Massachusetts to protect an FBI informant.

groups.name: Detroit Sleeper Cell Case
groups.description: Post-9/11 terrorism convictions in Detroit overturned in 2004 due to prosecutorial misconduct.

groups.name: Haymarket Affair Defendants
groups.description: Labor activists convicted following the 1886 Haymarket Square bombing in Chicago; three surviving defendants were pardoned in 1893.

groups.name: Kern County Child Abuse Cases
groups.description: Series of 1980s Satanic Panic child sex abuse prosecutions in Kern County, California, dozens of which were later overturned.

groups.name: Wenatchee Child Abuse Cases
groups.description: 1994–1995 child sex abuse witch-hunt prosecutions in Wenatchee, Washington resulting in numerous overturned convictions.
